cards.text: Picture it, friend. Paul, the apostle, just got dragged out of the temple by a mob, chained up by the commander of the Roman regiment, and CARRIED up the steps by soldiers (Acts 21:30-35). Right at the door of the barracks, he turns to the commander and asks, 'May I say something to you?'

cards.question: Paul's in chains and still asking to talk. What does the Roman commander ask him right back?

cards.text: Then the commander asks, 'Aren't you the Egyptian who incited a rebellion some time ago and led four thousand members of the Assassins into the wilderness?' You ever wave BIG at someone across a parking lot, and it is NOT who you thought?

cards.question: The commander wonders if Paul is that Egyptian rebel. How does Paul answer him?

answers.text: I am a Jew from Tarsus
I am a Greek from Athens
I am a trader from Alexandria

cards.text: Paul says Tarsus in Cilicia is no ordinary city. Friend, the man is in CHAINS and he still found time to brag on his hometown!

cards.question: Then Paul asks the commander to let him speak to the people.

cards.text: Permission granted. Paul stands on the steps and motions to the crowd, the SAME crowd that was just shouting for him to be taken away (Acts 21:36).

cards.question: When Paul motions to the crowd from the steps, the shouting only gets louder.
Paul spoke Greek with the Roman commander, but he addresses the crowd in ___.

cards.text: Paul starts his defense right there on the steps: 'Brothers and fathers, listen now to my defense before you.' When the crowd hears him speaking Hebrew, they get even MORE quiet.
Paul tells them he's a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia but raised right here in Jerusalem. He's showing his ID at the door before anybody even asks for it.

cards.question: Paul says he was educated in strict conformity to the law of their fathers. At whose feet did he learn?

cards.text: Gamaliel was a Pharisee and a teacher of the law (Acts 5:34). Paul says he was as zealous for God as any of them, and he persecuted this Way even to the death.
He even got letters from the high priest and the whole Council to bring believers in Damascus back to Jerusalem to be punished. So there he is, about noon, almost to Damascus, and SUDDENLY...

cards.question: Paul is on his way to Damascus at noon. What suddenly flashes around him?

answers.text: A great wind from the sea
A pillar of fire from above

cards.text: Paul falls to the ground and hears a voice: 'Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?' Saul is Paul's other name (Acts 13:9), and when somebody says your name TWICE, friend, you stop whatever you're doing.

cards.question: Paul asks the voice on the Damascus road, 'Who are You, Lord?' Who answers him?
Paul's companions on the Damascus road could understand the voice speaking to him.

cards.text: Paul asks, 'What should I do, Lord?' Jesus tells him to get up and go into Damascus, where he'll be told all that he's been appointed to do.

cards.question: Paul's companions have to lead him by the hand into Damascus.

cards.text: In Damascus there's a man named Ananias (not the Ananias of Acts 5:1), a devout observer of the law, highly regarded by all the Jews living there. Ananias comes and stands right beside Paul.

cards.question: Ananias says, 'Brother Saul,' and at that moment Paul gets his ___ back.

cards.text: Then Ananias says the God of their fathers has appointed Paul to know His will, to see the Righteous One and to hear His voice. The man who was hunting believers just got a WHOLE new job description.

cards.question: Ananias tells Paul he will be His ___ to everyone of what he has seen and heard.
Ananias asks Paul, 'And now what are you waiting for?' What does he tell Paul to do?

answers.text: Be baptized and wash his sins away
Go and report to the high priest
Stay hidden until the danger passes

cards.question: Later, back in Jerusalem, Paul is praying at the temple and falls into a trance. The Lord tells him to hurry and leave Jerusalem quickly. Why?

answers.text: The people won't accept his testimony
Ananias needs him back in Damascus
His work in Jerusalem is all done

cards.text: 'Lord,' Paul answers, 'they know very well that in one synagogue after another I imprisoned and beat those who believed in You.'

cards.question: Paul keeps reminding the Lord of his past. What does he say about Stephen, the Lord's witness?

answers.text: He watched over the garments of his killers
He tried to stop the crowd that killed him
He buried him outside the city walls

cards.question: Then the Lord tells Paul, 'Go! I will send you far away to the ___.'

cards.text: The crowd listens to Paul right up until that last line about the Gentiles. Then the volume comes BACK.

cards.question: The crowd stops listening when Paul says the Lord sent him to the Gentiles. What do they shout about Paul?

answers.text: That he is not fit to live
That he should be set free
That he should keep on speaking

cards.text: They're shouting, throwing off their cloaks and tossing dust into the air. Friend, I've seen some upset bakers, but I have NEVER seen anybody throw their apron AND the flour.

cards.question: With the crowd this wild, the commander has Paul brought into the barracks. What does he order next?

answers.text: That Paul be flogged and questioned
That Paul be handed back to the crowd
That Paul be locked up without food

cards.question: The commander wants to find out the reason the crowd is shouting against Paul.

cards.text: The soldiers stretch Paul out to strap him down. Right then, Paul has a question for the centurion standing there, a Roman officer.

cards.question: Paul asks the centurion, 'Is it lawful for you to flog a Roman ___ without a trial?'

cards.text: The centurion goes straight to the commander and tells him Paul is a Roman citizen. It's like snapping at the guy who cut in front of you in line, then watching him turn around, and he's your new BOSS.

cards.question: When the commander asks if he is a Roman citizen, Paul refuses to answer.

cards.text: Then the commander tells Paul he paid a high price for his citizenship. I bet he's ready to compare receipts.

cards.question: The commander paid a high price to become a Roman citizen. How did Paul become one?

answers.text: He paid an even higher price

cards.question: The men about to interrogate Paul step back at once, and the commander is ___ when he realizes he put a Roman citizen in chains.

cards.text: Hang on to your apron, friend. This story is still warming up in the oven.
